questions.stem: A 54-year-old woman has 2 months of worsening shortness of breath, orthopnea, and ankle swelling. One year ago she finished chemotherapy for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. During each infusion of one of the drugs, her urine turned red-orange for a day. She has no history of hypertension, diabetes, or coronary disease. Blood pressure is 102/66 mm Hg and pulse is 104/min. There are bibasilar crackles and an S3. Echocardiography shows dilation of all four chambers and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 30%. Endomyocardial biopsy shows vacuolated myocytes with loss of myofibrils. Which mechanism most likely explains her heart disease?
choices: Antibody blockade of HER2 signaling in cardiomyocytes
Inhibition of microtubule assembly in myocytes
Iron-dependent free radical injury to myocytes
Thiamine depletion that impairs myocyte energy production
Repeated coronary vasospasm causing small infarcts
questions.explanation: Red-orange urine during treatment for lymphoma points to an **anthracycline** such as **doxorubicin**. Anthracyclines form **iron-dependent free radicals** that damage myocyte membranes and myofibrils, causing a **dose-dependent, mostly irreversible dilated cardiomyopathy**; dexrazoxane, an iron chelator, can reduce this injury. HER2 blockade by trastuzumab also lowers the EF, but it is used for HER2-positive breast cancer, not lymphoma, and its damage is usually reversible without myofibril loss on biopsy.
questions.explanation_pt: Urina vermelho-alaranjada durante o tratamento de um linfoma indica uma **antraciclina**, como a **doxorrubicina**. As antraciclinas formam **radicais livres dependentes de ferro** que lesam as membranas e as miofibrilas dos miócitos, causando uma **cardiomiopatia dilatada dose-dependente e geralmente irreversível**; o dexrazoxano, um quelante de ferro, pode reduzir essa lesão. O bloqueio do HER2 pelo trastuzumabe também reduz a FE, mas ele é usado no câncer de mama HER2-positivo, e não no linfoma, e sua lesão costuma ser reversível, sem perda de miofibrilas na biópsia.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man has 1 year of increasing abdominal swelling, leg edema, and fatigue. He was treated for pulmonary tuberculosis 10 years ago. Blood pressure is 104/68 mm Hg and pulse is 96/min. Jugular venous pressure is high and rises further with inspiration. The liver is enlarged, and there is ascites. The lungs are clear. CT of the chest shows a thick, calcified pericardium. Echocardiography shows normal ventricular wall thickness and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 60%. Which additional finding is most likely on cardiac auscultation?
choices: An early diastolic sound heard just after S2
A late diastolic sound heard just before S1
A mid-systolic click followed by a late systolic murmur
Wide splitting of S2 that does not change with breathing
An opening snap followed by a low-pitched rumble at the apex
questions.explanation: Prior tuberculosis, a **calcified pericardium**, **Kussmaul sign** and right-sided congestion with normal walls mean **constrictive pericarditis**. The rigid pericardium lets the ventricles fill fast at first and then stops filling suddenly in early diastole, which makes a **pericardial knock** just after S2. A late diastolic S4 needs atrial contraction into a stiff ventricle, as in hypertrophy or restrictive disease; in constriction most filling is already done before the atrium contracts. An opening snap also comes after S2, but it belongs to mitral stenosis and is followed by a diastolic rumble.
questions.explanation_pt: Tuberculose prévia, **pericárdio calcificado**, **sinal de Kussmaul** e congestão direita com paredes normais indicam **pericardite constritiva**. O pericárdio rígido permite um enchimento ventricular rápido no início, que é interrompido de forma súbita no começo da diástole, gerando o **knock pericárdico** logo após a B2. A B4, no fim da diástole, exige contração atrial contra um ventrículo rígido, como na hipertrofia ou na doença restritiva; na constrição, quase todo o enchimento já ocorreu antes da contração atrial. O estalido de abertura também vem após a B2, mas pertence à estenose mitral e é seguido de ruflar diastólico.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old man with end-stage kidney disease has missed his hemodialysis sessions for 2 weeks. He has 3 days of sharp chest pain that improves when he sits up and leans forward. Temperature is 37.2°C, blood pressure is 146/88 mm Hg, and pulse is 92/min. There is no pulsus paradoxus. A scratchy, three-part rub is heard over the left sternal border. Laboratory results: blood urea nitrogen 132 mg/dL, creatinine 11.2 mg/dL, potassium 5.4 mEq/L, and bicarbonate 17 mEq/L. ECG shows sinus rhythm without peaked T waves. Echocardiography shows a small pericardial effusion with no collapse of the right heart chambers. Which is the most appropriate next step in management?
choices: Oral ibuprofen and colchicine
Pericardiocentesis
Intravenous calcium gluconate
Oral prednisone
Intensified hemodialysis
questions.explanation: Chest pain that improves when leaning forward and a **friction rub** in a patient with very high BUN who missed dialysis indicate **uremic pericarditis**. The cause is the retained uremic toxins, so the treatment is **more intensive dialysis**. Ibuprofen with colchicine is the usual treatment for viral pericarditis, but it does not remove the cause here, and colchicine is risky with kidney failure. Pericardiocentesis is for tamponade, which is absent (no pulsus paradoxus, no chamber collapse), and calcium gluconate is for hyperkalemia with ECG changes.
questions.explanation_pt: Dor torácica que melhora ao inclinar o tronco para a frente e **atrito pericárdico** em um paciente com ureia muito elevada que faltou à diálise indicam **pericardite urêmica**. A causa são as toxinas urêmicas retidas, então o tratamento é **diálise mais intensiva**. Ibuprofeno com colchicina é o tratamento habitual da pericardite viral, mas não remove a causa aqui, e a colchicina é arriscada na insuficiência renal. A pericardiocentese é para tamponamento, que está ausente (sem pulso paradoxal, sem colapso de câmaras), e o gluconato de cálcio é para hipercalemia com alterações no ECG.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old man had a transurethral resection of the prostate 5 weeks ago. Now he has 3 weeks of fever, fatigue, and poor appetite. Temperature is 38.3°C. There is a new holosystolic murmur at the apex. Three sets of blood cultures grow gram-positive cocci in pairs and short chains. The colonies show no hemolysis on blood agar. The organism grows in 6.5% sodium chloride and hydrolyzes esculin in the presence of bile. Which organism is most likely causing his infection?
choices: Streptococcus gallolyticus
Enterococcus faecalis
Staphylococcus epidermidis
Streptococcus sanguinis
Streptococcus agalactiae
questions.explanation: Endocarditis after a **urinary tract procedure** with nonhemolytic cocci that grow in **6.5% NaCl** and are **bile esculin positive** points to **enterococci**, such as *E. faecalis*. *S. gallolyticus* is also bile esculin positive and nonhemolytic, but it does **not grow in 6.5% NaCl**. *S. epidermidis* forms clusters and is typical of prosthetic valve infection.
questions.explanation_pt: Endocardite após **procedimento no trato urinário** com cocos não hemolíticos que crescem em **NaCl a 6,5%** e são **bile-esculina positivos** indica **enterococos**, como o *E. faecalis*. O *S. gallolyticus* também é bile-esculina positivo e não hemolítico, mas **não cresce em NaCl a 6,5%**. O *S. epidermidis* forma cachos e é típico da infecção de prótese valvar.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman has 5 weeks of low-grade fever, fatigue, and a 3-kg weight loss. She has had no recent dental, urinary, or surgical procedures. Temperature is 38.0°C. There is a new soft, decrescendo diastolic murmur at the left sternal border. Laboratory results: hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume 72 fL, ferritin 9 ng/mL, and leukocytes 11,800/mm³. Blood cultures grow nonhemolytic gram-positive cocci in chains that hydrolyze esculin in bile but do not grow in 6.5% sodium chloride. Echocardiography shows a vegetation on the aortic valve. Antibiotics are started. Which test is most important next to find the underlying source?
choices: Panoramic dental radiograph
Cystoscopy
Upper endoscopy
Colonoscopy
Bone marrow biopsy
questions.explanation: Nonhemolytic, bile esculin positive streptococci that do not grow in 6.5% NaCl are ***Streptococcus gallolyticus*** (*S. bovis*), and its endocarditis is strongly linked to **colorectal neoplasia**. The **iron deficiency anemia** (low MCV and ferritin) adds a second clue for a bleeding colon tumor, so **colonoscopy** is needed. Upper endoscopy can also find a cause of iron deficiency, but the organism points to the colon. A dental radiograph fits viridans streptococci, and cystoscopy fits enterococci after urinary procedures.
questions.explanation_pt: Estreptococos não hemolíticos, bile-esculina positivos, que não crescem em NaCl a 6,5% são o ***Streptococcus gallolyticus*** (*S. bovis*), e a endocardite por ele está fortemente associada a **neoplasia colorretal**. A **anemia ferropriva** (VCM e ferritina baixos) é uma segunda pista de um tumor de cólon que sangra, por isso a **colonoscopia** é necessária. A endoscopia digestiva alta também pode identificar uma causa de ferropenia, mas o organismo aponta para o cólon. A radiografia odontológica se aplica aos estreptococos do grupo viridans, e a cistoscopia aos enterococos após procedimentos urinários.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma has sudden weakness of his right arm and the right side of his face. He has had no fever or chills. Temperature is 36.8°C. A soft systolic murmur is heard at the apex. MRI of the brain shows small infarcts in several vascular territories. Echocardiography shows several small vegetations along the closure line of the mitral valve leaflets, without valve destruction. Three sets of blood cultures, drawn before any antibiotics, show no growth after 5 days. Which best describes the vegetations?
choices: Sterile deposits of fibrin and platelets
HACEK bacteria trapped in fibrin deposits
Fibrinoid deposits with immune complexes on both valve surfaces
Calcified nodules from degeneration of the valve
Fungal hyphae within a large thrombus
questions.explanation: Advanced cancer, especially **mucin-producing adenocarcinoma** such as pancreatic cancer, creates a **hypercoagulable state** that can cause **marantic (nonbacterial thrombotic) endocarditis**: small, **sterile fibrin-platelet vegetations** on the closure lines that embolize, here to the brain. HACEK organisms are a cause of culture-negative endocarditis, but they cause a true infection with fever and valve damage, which this afebrile patient does not have. Vegetations on both valve surfaces describe Libman-Sacks endocarditis in lupus.
questions.explanation_pt: O câncer avançado, especialmente o **adenocarcinoma produtor de mucina** como o de pâncreas, cria um **estado de hipercoagulabilidade** que pode causar **endocardite marântica (trombótica não bacteriana)**: vegetações pequenas e **estéreis de fibrina e plaquetas** nas linhas de fechamento, que embolizam, aqui para o cérebro. Os organismos do grupo HACEK são causa de endocardite com hemocultura negativa, mas causam infecção verdadeira, com febre e lesão valvar, o que este paciente afebril não tem. Vegetações nas duas faces da valva descrevem a endocardite de Libman-Sacks no lúpus.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old woman has sudden crushing chest pain and shortness of breath 2 hours after she learns that her son died in a car crash. Blood pressure is 112/74 mm Hg and pulse is 104/min. ECG shows ST elevation in leads V2 to V5. Troponin I is mildly elevated. Urgent coronary angiography shows no significant stenosis and no thrombus. Left ventriculography shows that the apex and mid-ventricle balloon outward and do not contract, while the base contracts strongly. The wall motion defect extends beyond the territory of any single coronary artery. Four weeks later, her wall motion is normal. Which mechanism most likely explains her condition?
choices: Thrombus on a ruptured coronary plaque
Autoantibodies against myocardial proteins
Viral infection with lymphocytic infiltration of the myocardium
Vasospasm of one epicardial coronary artery
Myocardial stunning from a surge of catecholamines
questions.explanation: Severe emotional stress, ST elevation, normal coronary arteries, and **apical ballooning** that recovers in weeks describe **takotsubo (stress) cardiomyopathy**. A **catecholamine surge** is thought to stun the myocardium temporarily. Coronary vasospasm can also cause ST elevation with normal angiography, but it affects the territory of one artery and usually causes brief attacks, not a large apical wall motion defect. Plaque rupture is excluded by the normal angiogram.
questions.explanation_pt: Estresse emocional intenso, supradesnivelamento do ST, coronárias normais e **balonamento apical** que se recupera em semanas descrevem a **cardiomiopatia de takotsubo (de estresse)**. Acredita-se que uma **descarga de catecolaminas** atordoe o miocárdio de forma temporária. O vasoespasmo coronariano também pode causar supradesnivelamento do ST com angiografia normal, mas afeta o território de uma só artéria e costuma causar crises breves, e não um grande defeito de contração apical. A ruptura de placa é excluída pela angiografia normal.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man has 3 days of chest pain, shortness of breath, and palpitations. Ten days ago he had fever, sore throat, and muscle aches that went away on their own. He takes no medications. Temperature is 37.9°C, blood pressure is 98/64 mm Hg, and pulse is 118/min. Laboratory results: troponin I markedly elevated, leukocytes 9,200/mm³ with 2% eosinophils, and C-reactive protein elevated. Echocardiography shows global hypokinesis, a left ventricular ejection fraction of 35%, and normal wall thickness. Coronary angiography is normal. An endomyocardial biopsy is done. Which finding is most likely?
choices: Myofiber disarray with interstitial fibrosis
Lymphocytic infiltrate with focal myocyte necrosis
Eosinophilic infiltrate with endocardial fibrosis
Noncaseating granulomas with giant cells
Extracellular deposits with apple-green birefringence
questions.explanation: A young adult with heart failure, chest pain and high troponin after a viral illness, with normal coronary arteries, has **viral myocarditis**, most often from **Coxsackie B**. Biopsy shows a **lymphocytic infiltrate** with **myocyte necrosis**. An eosinophilic infiltrate suggests hypersensitivity myocarditis or Löffler endocarditis, but he takes no drugs and his eosinophil count is normal. Myofiber disarray is hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, which has thick walls.
questions.explanation_pt: Um adulto jovem com insuficiência cardíaca, dor torácica e troponina elevada após uma doença viral, com coronárias normais, tem **miocardite viral**, mais frequentemente por **Coxsackie B**. A biópsia mostra **infiltrado linfocitário** com **necrose de miócitos**. Um infiltrado eosinofílico sugere miocardite de hipersensibilidade ou endocardite de Löffler, mas ele não usa medicamentos e sua contagem de eosinófilos é normal. O desarranjo das miofibras é da cardiomiopatia hipertrófica, que tem paredes espessas.
